Iteration Structures
Part 2: While Loops
While loops continue to execute for as
long as a condition remains True.

While Loops
While Loop: An iteration structure that repeatedly executes a code block as long as a
condition remains True.
Before each iteration, the condition is evaluated.
•
If the condition is True, the code block executes.
•
If the condition is False, the loop ends and the program continues.
Unlike a for loop, a while loop does not automatically know when it should stop.
The programmer is responsible for creating a condition that will eventually evaluate to
False.
If the condition never becomes False, the loop will continue running indefinitely.
Because of this, while loops provide more flexibility than for loops, but they also
require more care to avoid creating unintended infinite loops.
